question: Should exact requester adoption of descendant output terminally satisfy descendant delivery even if the requester's outward send later fails?
rationale: The patch deliberately treats internal requester consumption as durable delivery proof, changing the meaning of `delivery.status` for this case; source correctness alone cannot determine whether that is the intended product state model.

options.title: Treat requester consumption as delivered
options.body: Accept exact requester adoption as terminal descendant delivery proof while preserving consumption metadata for diagnostics.

options.title: Track consumption separately
options.body: Record requester consumption without ending external delivery eligibility until the requester result is delivered outward.

recommendation.title: Treat requester consumption as delivered
recommendation.body: Accept exact requester adoption as terminal descendant delivery proof while preserving consumption metadata for diagnostics.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal across the registry, announcement, lifecycle, and cron delivery boundaries makes this the best available owner for the cross-cutting state-model choice.
